issue.title: Nulloy Crashing on MacOs
issue.body:
Hello,

I really love Nulloy and have been using it for many years. However, I’ve always used it on Windows. I switched to a MacBook (Pro M3 - 18GB - Tahoe 26.2) about 2 months ago, and since then I’ve been experiencing this bug quite frequently.

Because I like the software so much and haven’t found any good alternatives, I decided to come directly to you to report this issue.

I often build DJ sets, so I receive a lot of tracks weekly that I need to preview quickly. With just a few clicks on different parts of a track, I can already evaluate things like the kick, bass, rhythm, etc. Because of that, I navigate very quickly between tracks and jump to different positions within them.

The issue is that when I click rapidly across different tracks and positions, after some time the software crashes. This never happens when I simply play a track normally without skipping through it.

So basically, the crash only occurs when I’m quickly switching between tracks and jumping around within them. After a while, the program crashes and I need to force quit it.

I’ve recorded a video showing the crash happening multiple times (around 5 times in a row). I’ve also tried reinstalling the software several times, but the issue persists.

Here is the Google Drive link with the screen recording:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/196ZeqngbLyRvEYuJ76WXR_2OoK55zf0e/view?usp=sharing

comments.body:
The warning is due the use of `QAbstractFileEngine`, which became private in Qt5.

`QAbstractFileEngine` enables support for compressed skins (`.nzs`). Alternative would be to use `QWebEngineUrlSchemeHandler`, but it depends on a huge `webenginecore` module.

I can think of disabling compressed skins support, which would remove the warning.
Actually, I hope I can use https://doc.qt.io/qt-5/qdesktopservices.html#setUrlHandler instead.

No, it will store the settings in the local directory. However, if you extract the archive under `C:\Program Files ...` then it will store the setting in `C:\Users\...\AppData\Roaming\Nulloy`

issue.title: Different icons (or color) for different type of files
issue.body:
Hi. Thanks for the 0.7 release, really works great.
Maybe for the future, you can set a different icon for each type of file: wav, mp3, etc. Maybe the same icon but in a different color should already help a lot when displaying lots of files within a folder.
Thanks again, great job!

comments.body:
Hi. Cannot promise anything, as there way too many audio formats out there. What I could probably do is to add a new info tag for playlist to print file name extension, in capital and not. So then you would arrange the tags order for example as 
MP3 | Track 1 (2:43)
AAC | Track 2 (3:13)
FLAC | Track 3 (4:23)
OGG | Track 4 (3:36)
Would this be any help?

Hi. Thanks for quicky reply.

That definetely would help. But thinking in the Explorer view (windows for ej.) if you change the color for just WAV format or MP3 format (the 2 more commons), that is enough for the most of us I think, you don't need to make an icon for each format. It's just a suggest.

I think the issue to you comes as Nulloy doesn't install, isn't it? It's a portable programm, so one has to associate file format to the programm.

But again, don't worry, it's just works really great as it is.

Thanks again.
Greets.

I'll make file extension tag in the next release. I'll think about colors for some later later version.

I have plans for Windows installer for version 1.0. Until then zip only ;)
Don't worry putting file extensión tags!, it already looks so sharp, clean and smooth, it would be a pitty! Leave the icons issue to version 1, then! :D

Added `%e` and `%E` file extension tags in 4fe9480, can be used as

```
%E | %f (%d)
```
